STATUS_2026-05-24: SUSPECT — superseded in part by docs/re/findings/state4-runtime-palette.json. Two specific claims here are believed wrong: (a) 'df85 = wroot file offset 0x22B7' — wbase E8-call-target math at 0x23DC and 0x27BD lands on thunk 0xDF85, which per the thunk-delta law resolves to wroot ~0x24E9, off by ~0x232 from this file's claim. (b) 'palette[5] = (170,255,0) yellow-green via WIZ6_MAIN matches user observation' — empirically the live DAC is EGA_DEFAULT (mcp__wiz6__dosbox_identify_palette distance 0 across saves 1, 2, 5, 10); palette[5] under EGA_DEFAULT is (170,0,170) magenta. User confirms engine renders yellow-on-black on the menu cursor, which is palette[14] under EGA_DEFAULT — so either attr is 14 not 5, OR the menu cursor uses a different render primitive than the one traced here. The 1bpp wfont0 sheet is reused across multiple engine primitives with different fg/bg semantics; this file likely traced one such primitive correctly but mis-identified it as the menu cursor.
summary: Decoded the engine's text-highlight path (df85 = wroot file offset 0x22B7 = 'ui_window_putchar_highlight'). The highlight encoding is: cell stores (char, attr<<4) — original attr in HIGH nibble, low nibble = 0. The blit-time dispatch at wroot 0x2C20 sees attr_low==0 and routes to ega.drv slot 1 (the '1bpp text' slot at file 0x19A, runtime 0x29A). Slot 1 is a per-plane bit-selector that uses wfont0 (1bpp font, 1024 bytes total, 8 bytes/glyph, indexed by char code) as the only glyph source. For each EGA plane P (0..3), it tests bit (4+P) of ah; if SET, writes NOT(wfont0[char][row]) to that plane; if CLEAR, writes 0 (from a fixed all-zero buffer at runtime cs:0x292) to that plane. Bits 4..7 of ah hold the original attr value. Net per-pixel color: foreground (wfont0_bit=1) -> palette index 0 (black); background (wfont0_bit=0) -> palette index = attr_low_nibble. For attr=5 (the menu-selected case after negation of -5), this gives black-on-palette5 which in WIZ6_MAIN is (170,255,0) — the 'yellow' the user sees. The 'negated' flag derived from sign of input attr is stored as a per-cell marker bit (0x80 in the dirty map at [cs:0x1b60]) but does NOT affect the rendered color — the NOT-invert in slot 1 is gated on the second pushed arg [bp+0x8] (the dirty-map cell byte) being non-zero, which it always is after the window-index match test. So df85 with positive attr=3 and df85 with negative attr=-3 produce IDENTICAL pixels. The sign is purely a 'mark this cell as highlighted in the dirty map' signal for upstream code (probably the cursor-tracking logic).
key_insight: wfont0 (1bpp) is the highlight renderer's ONLY glyph source. wfont1..wfont4 are NOT consulted on the highlight path, despite tile-mode windows storing arbitrary char codes. The engine renders the SAME 1bpp glyph shapes for highlight as for any other 1bpp-text-mode primitive. The 'tile mode' assumption from the prior wfont-tile-system finding — that all text in tile-mode windows uses wfont1..wfont4 — is wrong for highlight cells; those use wfont0.
method: Static ndisasm of (1) df85 at wroot file 0x22B7 (=image 0x22B7 after stripping 0x200 MZ header), (2) ega.drv slot 1 at file 0x19A, (3) wroot blit dispatch at file 0x2C20-2C6E showing where [cs:0x1b8a] is reached (cell.attr.low_nibble==0 path), (4) wroot driver-init at file 0x1F40-1FA6 showing ega.drv loads at offset 0x100 of its runtime segment and the slot-table fixup at wroot 0x1B86-1BCC. Cross-checked against the call site in FUN_025c (wbase_menu_select_loop, wbase 0x025C+0x3CC..0x3E9) which pushes attr=-param_8=-5 for the selected option. Palette mapping verified against packages/data/src/palettes/wiz6-main.ts (palette index 5 = (170,255,0)).

df85_function.attribute_transform: If sign bit of incoming attr word is set, negate to get |attr| and set negated_flag = 1. Cell-write stores char in low byte, |attr|<<4 in high byte (low nibble of attr byte = 0, which is the blit-time signal to dispatch to slot 1 instead of slot 2). Negated_flag is also OR'd as bit 7 into the cell's dirty-map byte at [cs:0x1b60]:row*0x28+col.
df85_function.dispatched_to: ega.drv slot 1 via far call [cs:0x1b8a]. Slot table at wroot file 0x1B86; slot 1's entry is at 0x1B8A (4 bytes = offset 0x0103 + segment placeholder). The segment is patched at startup by the driver loader (wroot 0x1F76-1F86) with [cs:0x1b84] = driver_segment. Inside ega.drv, the slot's body is at file offset 0x19A (= runtime offset 0x29A, since the driver image is read into its segment at offset 0x100).

blit_dispatch.summary: The per-cell blit loop at 0x2C20 also reaches slot 1 for any cell whose attr-byte low nibble is zero. So even cells df85 wrote earlier get re-rendered via slot 1 on subsequent dirty-cell sweeps (with the SAME inputs: ax = cell_word, [bp+8] = dirty-map byte which is non-zero because the cell's window index just matched).

highlight_renderer.name: ega_drv_slot1_text_1bpp_per_plane_selector

args.al: char code (0..127, used to index wfont0 at char*8)
args.ah: attr-byte from cell: original attr in HIGH nibble (bits 4-7), low nibble must be 0 for slot dispatch to reach here
args.stack_bp+6: ignored (df85 pushes the negated flag here; slot never reads it)
args.stack_bp+8: WORD: when non-zero, plane writes are NOT-inverted. This is the dirty-map byte from the caller; always non-zero in practice because a window-index test just passed. Effectively means: 'always NOT-invert under df85/blit dispatch'.
args.stack_bp+0xA: segment-like word. dh & 0x40 -> alt branch at 0x380 (not used on normal call paths).

highlight_renderer.color_transform:
Per-pixel per-plane formula. Let attr = (ah >> 4) & 0x0F (the original attr value held in the high nibble of cell.attr by df85). Let w = wfont0[char][row][col_bit] (1bpp, 1 if foreground stroke at this pixel, 0 if background). Let inv = ([bp+8] != 0) which is ALWAYS TRUE under df85/blit dispatch. Then for each plane P in 0..3: plane_bit = (attr & (1<<P)) ? (inv ? !w : w) : 0. Output palette index = sum(plane_bit_P << P) for P in 0..3.

With inv=1 (the only case observed in real call paths): plane_bit = (attr & (1<<P)) ? !w : 0. So:
  - If w=1 (foreground stroke): all plane_bits = 0 -> output = 0 (BLACK).
  - If w=0 (background): plane_bit = (attr_bit_P) ? 1 : 0 -> output = attr.

Net: highlight cells render as 'wfont0 glyph in palette-0 (black) on a palette-attr background'.
highlight_renderer.source_a_is_zero: The 'bit clear' branch's source is cs:0x292 (a 'fixed 8-byte pattern'). At runtime, ega.drv is loaded at offset 0x100 of its segment, so cs:0x292 corresponds to ega.drv file offset 0x192. Confirmed by xxd: bytes 0x192..0x199 are all 0x00. This is an uninitialized buffer the code uses as a 'plane all-zero' source.
highlight_renderer.negated_flag_is_color_irrelevant: The negated_flag set by df85 (when called with negative attr) is pushed at bp+6 in the slot 1 callee. Slot 1 never reads [bp+6]. The NOT-invert is gated on [bp+8] (the dirty-map byte), which is always non-zero on real call paths. So passing -3 vs +3 to df85 produces identical pixels. The flag IS recorded as bit 7 of the dirty-map byte for upstream tracking (probably cursor/selection state), just not consulted by the renderer.

ts_implementation.summary: Given (char, attr_byte_in_cell) and the wfont0 1bpp font, produce per-pixel palette indices for an 8x8 cell.
pseudocode: // Cell format produced by df85:
//   char_byte = char (0..127)
//   attr_byte = (original_attr_lo_nibble) << 4   // low nibble is 0
// Detection: if (cell.attr_byte & 0x0F) === 0 && cell.attr_byte !== 0, this is a highlight cell.
// (attr_byte === 0 is a normal empty/no-render cell, separately handled.)
function renderHighlightCell(char: number, attrByte: number, wfont0: Uint8Array): number[] /* 64 palette indices, row-major */ {
const attr = (attrByte >> 4) & 0x0F;   // recover original attr value (0..15)
const out = new Array<number>(64);
for (let y = 0; y < 8; y++) {
const glyphByte = wfont0[char * 8 + y];   // 1bpp scanline, bit 7 = leftmost pixel
for (let x = 0; x < 8; x++) {
const w = (glyphByte >> (7 - x)) & 1;   // foreground bit
// Engine ALWAYS NOT-inverts on df85 path:
out[y * 8 + x] = w ? 0 : attr;
return out;
// Equivalent simpler form of the color override the task description proposed:
// highlightColorOverride does not exist as a (file_color -> palette_index) table here, because the highlight
// renderer does NOT read wfont1..wfont4 (which have 4bpp 'file colors'). It reads wfont0 (1bpp) and emits
// {0, attr} only. If the calling code wants to layer the 4bpp wfontN glyph back in, the closest emulation
// is: ignore the 4bpp glyph entirely, look up wfont0[char] as a 1bpp mask, and emit (1 -> 0, 0 -> attr).
// For the menu case attr=5 -> attr_byte_in_cell = 0x50:
//   wfont0 stroke (1) -> 0 -> WIZ6_MAIN[0] = (0,0,0)  BLACK
//   wfont0 background (0) -> 5 -> WIZ6_MAIN[5] = (170,255,0)  YELLOW-GREEN
// This matches the user's observed 'black on yellow' for the selected menu option.
ts_implementation.viewer_port_note: The current port hardcodes `{ 1: 0, 8: 14 }` as a file-color->palette-index override on top of the 4bpp wfont3 panel-variant glyph. That approximation works visually only because file color 1 happens to be the stroke color and file color 8 the background color of the wfont3 panel-uppercase glyphs, and palette 14 in the port's palette happens to land near palette 5 in WIZ6_MAIN. The ENGINE-correct behavior is to discard the wfont3 glyph entirely on highlight cells and rasterize wfont0[char] as a 1bpp mask producing (0 if stroke, attr if background). The wfont3 4bpp glyph is conceptually irrelevant on highlight cells — df85 doesn't care which 4bpp font the cell originally referenced.

menu_selected_case.input: df85(menu_text_window, 'C', attr = -5)  // 'C' from 'CHARACTER MENU' selected option
trace: df85 detects sign bit, negates -> 0x0005, sets negated_flag = 1
slot 1 plane tests: ah & 0x10=1 (P0 set), ah & 0x20=0 (P1 clear), ah & 0x40=1 (P2 set), ah & 0x80=0 (P3 clear)
[bp+8] = pushed dirty-byte (non-zero, =1|0x80=0x81), so NOT-invert branch taken on all SET planes
P0 = NOT(w), P1 = 0, P2 = NOT(w), P3 = 0
-> stroke pixels: 0 (BLACK in WIZ6_MAIN), background pixels: 5 (YELLOW-GREEN (170,255,0))
menu_selected_case.result: MATCHES the user's observed 'black on yellow' visual. Note that 'yellow' here is palette-index-5 = (170,255,0), which is a yellow-green / chartreuse, not the warm yellow at palette index 14 = (170,170,0). The viewer's hardcoded `{1:0, 8:14}` override should be replaced with `{1:0, 8:5}` if patching the current 4bpp approximation, OR replaced entirely with a wfont0-based 1bpp mask render for engine-correct behavior.

other_attr_examples.result: attr stays positive (no neg), cell_attr_byte = 0x60, ah & 0x10=0, ah & 0x20=1 (P1), ah & 0x40=1 (P2), ah & 0x80=0. Bg pixels -> palette index 6 = (0,255,0) bright green. Stroke -> black. So: black-on-green.
cell_attr_byte = 0x30, plane tests give P0=1, P1=1, P2=0, P3=0. Bg -> palette 3 = (170,85,170) magenta/light-purple. Stroke -> black. So: black-on-magenta.
Same as the main-menu selection visual: black-on-(170,255,0). The negated_flag is set in the dirty-map (bit 7) but doesn't change pixels.

validation.negation_does_not_affect_color: Confirmed by static analysis. df85 with positive attr=N and df85 with attr=-N produce identical cell.attr_byte (= N<<4) and the slot 1 dispatch sees [bp+8]!=0 in both cases (because the dirty-map byte is always non-zero post-window-match), so the NOT branch is always taken. The 'negated' encoding is a marker for the cell-tracking logic upstream (probably menu cursor/selection state), not a render-time flag.

open_questions.claim: Slot 1 has an alternate path entered when ([bp+0xA] high byte & 0x40) is non-zero, jumping to 0x380. This path is not exercised by df85 (which pushes ds = ordinary heap segment). Possibly a 'render to non-EGA target' or 'render to back-buffer-only' variant. Not investigated further as it's irrelevant to the highlight visual.

The negated_flag bit (0x80) df85 OR's into the dirty-map byte at [cs:0x1b60]:offset has SOME consumer (otherwise df85 wouldn't bother setting it). Candidates: (a) cursor blink toggle logic — re-render the highlighted cell each tick; (b) selection-state read-back when user presses Enter; (c) a 'restore prior cell' undo. Not investigated.

wroot 0x2C66 also calls slot 1 (from the blit loop). The blit pushes [bp-0x12] as the third arg and the dirty-map byte (kept in [es:si]) as the second arg. Both arguments are 'arbitrary but typically non-zero', so the rendered output is the same as df85's output for the same cell. Conclusion: slot 1 has effectively one observable behavior in this codebase: 'wfont0 NOT-mask producing {0 if stroke, attr if bg}'.

A cell with attr_byte = 0x00 (low nibble 0 AND high nibble 0) takes the highlight path but renders with attr=0 -> output = 0 for BOTH stroke and bg = all black. This is consistent with 'empty cell = blank black tile'. Empty cells in the cell array are stored as attr=0, and the blit at 0x2C33 jumps to the highlight call regardless. In practice the wbase code uses ed5a (ui_window_clear) with attr=3 to pre-fill cells (giving the gray wfont3 0x20 tile), so attr=0 is rare except for genuinely-empty regions.

implications_for_port: TileWindow rendering of highlight cells should ignore the 4bpp wfont3 glyph (or whichever wfont the original char/attr resolved to before df85) and instead render a 1bpp wfont0[char] mask: stroke -> palette[0], background -> palette[attr_low_nibble_of_high_nibble].
The cell encoding for highlight cells is (char, attr<<4). The viewer's tile-renderer can detect highlight cells by `(cell.attr & 0x0F) === 0 && cell.attr !== 0`.

Replacing the current hardcoded `{ 1: 0, 8: 14 }` override: the engine-correct color is `{ stroke: 0, background: 5 }` for the WIZ6_MAIN palette in attr=5 highlights — note that's palette index 5 = (170,255,0), NOT palette index 14 = (170,170,0). The current viewer's palette-14 yellow is visually close but slightly off; the engine renders the yellow-GREEN (170,255,0) for menu highlights.
wfont0.ega is 1024 bytes / 128 glyphs / 8 bytes each. The viewer probably already extracts this somewhere; if not, decoding is trivial (no compression).
Generalize to other df85 attrs: any (char, attr) where attr is 1..15 produces a black-on-palette[attr] highlight. The full table is just `palette[0..15]` for backgrounds, always with black strokes.

Negation of input attr is a 'mark dirty' signal, not a color signal. Port should treat df85(_, _, attr) and df85(_, _, -attr) identically for rendering. If the port needs the marker bit for cursor blink or interaction logic, store it separately in the TileWindow cell metadata.

cross_references.wfont_tile_system_finding: docs/re/findings/wfont-tile-system.json — its claim 'highlight_path_attr_minus_5: df85 shifts attr to high nibble, blit takes [cs:0x1b8a] empty-cell path' is CORRECT in the shift-and-dispatch step, but its characterization of the renderer as 'a DIFFERENT rendering primitive that uses the HIGH nibble for inverse-video / XOR-fill' is incomplete — the renderer is the wfont0 1bpp per-plane selector described here, not an XOR-fill.
cross_references.wbase_state4_draw_trace_finding: docs/re/findings/wbase-state4-draw-trace.json — describes the state-4 menu loop. The df85 call for the selected option happens inside FUN_025c (wbase_menu_select_loop), invoked from FUN_2b36 (state-4 entry) at wbase 0x2CCB with the 8th arg = 5 = the highlight attr.
